newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly lower on weak basis, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly lower on weak basis, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly lower on declining cash basis markets, the early vestiges of seasonal harvest pressure and on long liquidation in the September contract, traders said.
Dry U.S. Midwest weather lent pressure to corn while underpinning soybeans.
"The weather is supportive for beans but weather is fine for corn," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soybean futures were higher and helped underpin the corn market.
Drier-than-desired weather in the Midwest and some outlooks for cold weather to move into the Midwest by the weekend boosted soybeans.

Traders said talk that Farmers Commodities Corp later Tuesday would release a crop estimate also weighed on the market. Also FCC sold three million bushels of December and Merrill Lynch Futures sold 2.5 million bushels of December, the traders said.
Corn closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower to five cents higher, with September down 3-3/4 cents per bushel at $3.66-3/4 a bushel.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 37,500 contracts, down from 41,321 Friday.
U.S.A. Trading sold 200 December $2.90 puts and Farmers Commodities Corp bought 150 December $3.50 calls, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 9,000 contracts, up from 8,813 Friday.
